claims.claim: Oklo addresses the firm-power bottleneck for electricity-intensive infrastructure through compact advanced nuclear, but the Groves criticality milestone is an execution analog rather than proof of commercial Aurora deployment.
Successor bottlenecks are licensing, fuel availability, construction repeatability, financing and customer commissioning; solving reactor physics alone does not remove them.

factors.name: alignment2036
factors.basis: Firm low-carbon generation addresses rising electricity demand from compute and industrial loads.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Need for firm power is durable, while first-of-a-kind licensing/fuel/construction pathways remain execution-sensitive.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Gas, renewables plus storage, grid expansion and other nuclear designs can satisfy portions of the same need.

risks.risk: Commercial value depends on regulatory, fuel, construction and commissioning milestones beyond demonstrated test-reactor operation.

causalEdges.mechanism: 24/7 electricity demand rewards dense dispatchable generation where grid capacity is constrained
causalEdges.falsifier: cheaper substitutes satisfy reliability and permitting needs before Aurora deployment

causalEdges.mechanism: operating experience can reduce technical and project uncertainty
causalEdges.falsifier: Aurora licensing/construction fails to translate despite Groves execution

unknowns.unknown: Commercial Aurora schedule, repeatable construction cost and realized unit economics remain unproven.

claims.claim: The principal thesis hazard is extrapolation from a test-reactor milestone to commercial Aurora economics; first criticality demonstrates capability but does not establish licensing, cost, schedule or fleet repeatability.
Accelerated project spending can advance readiness but also raises financing and dilution risk if commercial milestones slip because durable commercial cash flow is not yet demonstrated.

factors.name: financingRisk
factors.basis: First-of-a-kind nuclear development is capital intensive before durable commercial cash generation.

factors.name: substitutionRisk
factors.basis: Alternative firm generation, storage/grid solutions and competing reactor designs can compete for the same customers.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: A test-reactor milestone should not be treated as proof of commercial fleet economics.

risks.risk: Licensing, fuel, construction and capital needs can delay commercialization and increase dilution/financing dependence.
Competitive power solutions may improve faster than Aurora's time-to-market.

causalEdges.mechanism: pre-revenue spending persists while cash-flow timing moves outward
causalEdges.falsifier: timely licensing and project execution produce contracted commercial cash flows before funding stress emerges

contradictions.claim: Concrete nuclear execution signal versus unproven commercial economics
contradictions.resolution: Groves reduces one dimension of technical execution uncertainty but does not resolve Aurora licensing, cost or fleet economics.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not establish Aurora unit economics, final commercial schedule or probability-weighted licensing outcomes.
